RE N19 — raw natural-forced-position ledger and declared 4M reference sensitivity (074516Z). The identical 128 next-decision histories were searched cold at go softnodes 4000000 after ucinewgame/isready with the same 24 options; full histories were supplied. All reference PVs and moves were legal. All the timed trials had already finished before adding the larger referee. Over 236 common finite observations of 256, next-position CP discrepancy to the new reference was 183.52 baseline, 279.92 when skipping forced search at unchanged next-move time (+96.40 [52.88,147.81]), 149.67 when transferring all the saved time to the next move (−33.84 [−63.67,−8.57]). Move agreement 67.58%, 63.67%, 68.36%; paired changes −3.91pp [−11.33,3.52] and +0.78pp [−6.64,8.20]. This continues to demonstrate both lost information and real value from reinvesting time; the larger CP reference still shares Forge's evaluator/search. Unlike a whole-game timed match, the artificial full transfer commits every saved millisecond immediately. Use all comparisons as diagnosis, not an Elo claim.

Reproduction detail: 073208Z and 074516Z define source games, panels and phases. For a chosen root at N recorded plies, send ucinewgame/isready; starting at 8 for White or 9 for Black and stepping by 2, use go softnodes 2000 on each actual same-side prefix before N, with no opponent computation in that worker. Advance the board along the recorded line. Repeat this prefill for each timed arm. Rotate baseline-before-fast vs fast-before-baseline by shuffling [baseline,fast] with Python Random(202611230732+gameID+100000*rep), then run the reallocated arm. No-op controls at indices 0,16,...112 require exact equality in chosen move, score, depth and nodes across two full independent refills. The median forced elapsed time was 301.72 ms, the 10th/90th percentiles 245.73/484.69; actual timing and clock move choices vary by host. The 4M bootstrap uses the same game-cluster algorithm and seed as the 512k report.
